role.title: Equipment Services Technician
role.schedule: Sunday–Thursday, 2:00 pm – 11:30 pm (2nd shift, 6% shift differential)

mustSell: 5+ years repairing / troubleshooting automated manufacturing or distribution lines
3-phase 480V industrial electrical, conduit, motor control circuits
CMMS or SAP for work orders, parts, hours
Electrical / mechanical / pneumatic troubleshooting under production pressure
Microsoft Suite for documentation and communication
Comfortable standing/walking a full shift and filling in across shifts
preferred: Allen-Bradley / Rockwell PLC, HMI, RSLogix 500/5000, Studio 5000
Robotics on automated packaging / pharmacy lines
dayInLife: Check sensors and walk the line before/during production
Respond to radio service calls quickly; restore uptime
Maintain pill dispensers and mail-order pharmacy automation
Work work orders in CMMS/SAP; track parts and labor hours
Support install, setup, and prototyping of improvement projects

likelyQuestions.q: Walk me through how you troubleshoot a machine that suddenly stops on the line.
likelyQuestions.intent: Structured method under pressure — safety first, then isolate electrical/mechanical/pneumatic/controls.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Situation: unexpected stoppage on a high-throughput line. Task: restore safely and fast. Action: lockout/tagout if needed, check e-stops/sensors/air/PLC faults, use prints/HMI. Result: root cause + uptime + documentation.

likelyQuestions.q: Tell me about a time you diagnosed a 480V / motor control issue.
likelyQuestions.intent: Prove real industrial electrical experience, not just swapping parts.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Mention verifying power, contactor/overload, VFDs, phase imbalance, grounding, and when you escalate vs. fix yourself.

likelyQuestions.q: How do you use CMMS or SAP day to day?
likelyQuestions.intent: They want documented, prioritized maintenance — not hero firefighting only.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Open WO → diagnose → parts issue → labor hours → close with notes that help the next tech.

likelyQuestions.q: Have you worked with Allen-Bradley / Studio 5000 / RSLogix?
likelyQuestions.intent: Preferred PLC stack for this site. Be honest about depth.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Describe reading ladder/tags, forcing carefully, trending faults, coordinating with controls engineers, never downloading blindly.

likelyQuestions.q: This role is Sun–Thu 2nd shift with occasional Saturday OT. Are you flexible?
likelyQuestions.intent: Hard schedule requirement — answer clearly yes if true.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Confirm availability explicitly; mention prior shift experience if you have it.

likelyQuestions.q: Describe maintaining pneumatic systems on packaging or automation equipment.
likelyQuestions.intent: Pharmacy lines use lots of air: cylinders, valves, vacuum, regulators.
likelyQuestions.starHint: Leak checks, solenoid valves, pressure setpoints, dirty filters, sticky cylinders, interlocks tied to sensors.

likelyQuestions.q: How do you prioritize when multiple machines are down and production is waiting?
likelyQuestions.starHint: Safety → bottleneck/throughput impact → quick restores vs. long repairs → communicate ETA on radio.
Tie hands-on automation skills to reliable medication fulfillment and patient impact; emphasize ownership and learning.

technicalFlashcards.talkTrack: Industrial distribution voltage. Be ready to discuss LOTO, PPE, verifying absence of voltage, phase rotation, and motor starters/overloads.
Control power vs. power circuit: start/stop, interlocks, contactors, overloads, aux contacts, and how a failed sensor can drop out a run permissive.
Use fault codes and HMI alarms first. Trace inputs/outputs, check sensor status bits, review recent program changes, document tag/fault before clearing.
Compressed air quality and pressure stability matter. Isolate circuit, verify regulator/gauge, listen for leaks, check valve actuation and cylinder cushions.
Daily sensor checks catch misalignment, dirty optics, loose mounts, and drift before they cause nuisance stops or bad counts.
Wyatt's proof: Navy SKED as CMMS (schedule, spot checks, closeout) plus parts program. Work order hygiene: problem, root cause, parts, time, follow-up. Ask which CMMS/SAP Charlotte uses.
Accuracy and uptime are clinical-adjacent. Emphasize careful calibration, cleanliness, change control, and escalating software/controls issues properly.
Respect interlocks and safety circuits. Know teach pendant basics, collision recovery, and when to call OEM/robotics support.

answerFormulas.name: Troubleshoot formula
steps: Define the symptom precisely (what, when, alarms, last change)
Read HMI/PLC faults and sensor states
Isolate mechanical vs electrical vs pneumatic vs controls
Fix, test in manual then auto, monitor
Document in CMMS and communicate on radio

answerFormulas.name: STAR for maintenance stories
steps: Result: uptime restored, scrap avoided, PM improvement
